entries.original: Hephaestus on GPT-6.2 models sends one prompt instead of two: the GPT-6.2 core stands alone there, so the Hephaestus role is no longer appended after it. Other models keep the role, and switching models in a session drops or restores it. On a real request the system prompt goes from 9,211 to 4,300 tokens (`o200k_base`). The refusal-is-final rule is now stated once inside the model-core frame for every agent that carries it instead of at the end of the role, so it survives without the role and is never doubled by a model core that states it. entries.original: **`omo remote` takes a device by the name its table prints.** The session verbs (`open`, `send`, `model`, `interrupt`, `close`) accept a device's id, its name (compared as thread names are) or a unique id prefix, through the same resolver `thread_create` uses, and their output names the device by its id. entries.original: Creating a thread on another of your devices (`thread_create` with `device`, `omo remote open`) is faster. The create used to make four round trips over the relay: it looked up the device's engine endpoint, opened the session, attached to it, and named it. Now it makes two. The endpoint is looked up once per device, nothing attaches to the new session, and the name goes straight to it. entries.original: `thread_create` reopens a closed thread on another device again. It failed with `EISDIR`: the account listing names a session's working folder, never its session file, and that folder was sent to the other device as the file to open (a row with no path sent its working folder too). The reopen now opens the file the close was told by that device, or else asks the device which file carries the thread's id; a device that cannot say answers a typed refusal naming it (`unsupported` for an engine without the lookup, `not_found`, or `ambiguous_target`). A thread this device closed no longer lists as `live` while the listing catches up, and a reopen answers `ok` only once the reopened session can be reached, so the next tool call no longer answers `not_resumable`. ([#14179](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14179), fixes [#14170](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14170)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))

entries.original: `thread_send` to a thread on another device that is not running answers at once instead of waiting about 60 seconds for `unsupported` (`daemon_unavailable`). The device holding it is asked first, whether or not this device can wake it there: a thread it holds no session file for is `not_found` (as the refused reopen says), one it runs is delivered to (also when it was reopened elsewhere since this device last listed it, under whatever key it runs under now), and one it only has on disk is woken when this device can wake it there, else `not_resumable`, naming the reopen as the next step. A device without the wake capability counts as unable to wake. entries.original: `thread_create` (and `omo remote open`) on another device now opens the thread only on that device's own engine (the primary engine endpoint its device service names), never on the first endpoint listed. Before this, a thread could land on an owner shard or on another registered agent dir's older engine, which then refused every cross-device `thread_send` as unsupported (`method_unclassified`). When the device names no primary, because its own engine is not listed, the create now fails `host_unavailable` with reason `no_primary_endpoint` before anything opens, even if only one other endpoint is listed. The next action says to start or restart omo on that device, and to update the device service on both devices if that does not help (a device service older than 0.1.11 cannot name a primary; behind such a local service a device's lone endpoint is still used). ([#14200](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14200), fixes [#14195](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14195)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))

entries.original: When another device refuses a `thread_send` or `thread_handoff` because the chain went past that device user's thread chain limit (`threads.chainCountLimit`), the tool now answers `chain_count_limit`, naming the device and the setting, instead of `unsupported` with advice to update omo on that device. A queued delivery to a session there that is not running maps a chain-limit refusal from that device's gateway store to the same code, with the chain count and the limit, and the receiving consumer now passes on the store's own refusal reason (for example `sender_not_allowed`) instead of the coarse code. ([#12766](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12766)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))

entries.original: **A send to another device whose state read gets no answer can be retried right away.** When the `get_state` read that a steer to another device starts with ends without an answer, `thread_send` now reports `host_unavailable` (nothing was sent there, retry is safe) instead of `idempotency_uncertain`, and a retry under the same `idempotency_key` reads the target again instead of replaying that failure; a send that fails before its record leaves this device keeps no receipt. entries.original: **A delivery message without a valid id no longer inherits the previous sender's reply allowance.** A `session_control_delivery` whose `delivery_id` is not a string is malformed: after a final answer it starts a new group with nobody approved, and while work is running it joins the work without adding a sender or changing the hop - it no longer passes as a turn the engine started (which kept the earlier group's allowance). The same-account bound of the reply allowance is stated where the rule runs (`component.ts` `noteInput` and the thread `AGENTS.md`), not only in the release notes. ([#13134](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13134)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))

entries.original: Memory sync: a join, enable or passkey recovery that already pinned the account is no longer reported as failed when the follow-up root-change check cannot read the local retired pins. entries.original: Memory sync works again after a recovery phrase is set up. The sync engine's requests (batches, objects, uploads, sync state and the event stream), the device-list read and the account reads now declare the client contract version and the recovery-phrase capability, as the account and pairing requests already did. entries.original: Memory sync no longer stops for good when its first start fails. A start that fails (for example another omo process holding the account's credential lock past the 15 s wait) or gets stuck is retried on the same backoff as a waiting start, 15 s doubling to five minutes. A stuck start is named in the log, and the first successful start logs "memory sync started", so a log shows whether sync is running (#13701). ([#13706](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13706)) ([#14097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14097))

entries.original: **Scripts can create, interrupt, close, rename and re-model threads through the thread SDK.** `createThreadSdk(...)` from `runtime/thread-sdk/sdk.js` now has `create`, `interrupt`, `close`, `rename` and `set_model`. A script acts as itself, not as a session, so `self` answers `caller_context_missing` and a thread it creates records no creator session. entries.original: Memory sync can be turned off on one device. `omo sync disable` turns it off for the device it runs on: that device stops sending and receiving memory, memory already on it stays, and the account's other devices keep syncing. `omo sync enable` turns it on again without a new approval. An OmO session already running on that device stops syncing when its sync next reports a change, or at its next start, and a process that turns sync on again starts the engines it had stopped right away. For the desktop, the engine answers `omo.memory.sync.disable` with `{ kind: "off" }` or a typed problem, and lists `"disable"` in `omo.memory.sync.features`; turning off from the desktop app needs an app release that carries the matching request. ([#14121](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14121))
